title: Onboarding criteria for customer-managed KMS/HSM and audit retention
creator: Asha Patel
description: Purpose: Define clear, testable onboarding acceptance criteria for customers bringing their own keying infrastructure (KMS or HSM) and requiring extended audit retention and SSO/RBAC mapping in Private/VPC deployments. This ticket is a product-level acceptance criteria and sign-off checklist to be used by Solutions, Security, and CS during customer onboarding and by Engineering/Infra for gating releases. Scope: - KMS/HSM key provisioning and rotation workflows (BYOK, customer-managed keys) - CMK access controls and least-privilege mappings - SSO/SAML identity federation and attributes mapping for RBAC - Audit log collection, tamper-resistance, and retention policy configuration (configurable retention windows) - Operational runbooks for key compromise, rotation, and emergency recovery Out of scope: HSM hardware procurement guidance for customers, pricing model changes, and non-private (hosted API) flows.
acceptance_criteria: Customer-managed KMS/HSM can be registered via the onboarding flow with documented steps and a validation handshake (test encrypt/decrypt) verified in staging.
Key usage policy is enforced: service principals used by Redwood runtime have documented least-privilege IAM roles and IAM policies validated by Security.
Automatic rotation verification: rotation can be scheduled by customer and a successful rotation test (re-encrypt/re-decrypt a sample object) is executed and logged.
HSM attestation (if used) is captured and stored in onboarding artifacts; customers can choose FIPS-compliant HSMs; attestation report attached.
SSO/SAML onboarding: identity provider can be connected, SAML attributes (email, groups, role) mapped to Redwood RBAC roles and tested with a canary user.
RBAC mapping supports at minimum: Viewer, Operator, Admin with audit-level granularity for token issuance and key access.
Audit logs include key events (key create, rotate, destroy, access), SSO login events, admin RBAC changes, and are configurable for retention up to 365 days.
Audit export: logs can be exported to customer-owned storage (S3-like) or forwarded to customer SIEM with signed delivery proofs; export tests in onboarding must pass.
Security sign-off: Product Security and Infra Security must approve a checklist runbook and a verification report for the specific customer.
Operational acceptance: runbooks for key compromise, emergency rotation, and rollback are documented and exercised in a tabletop run before GA onboarding.
Legal/compliance: required data processing addenda and export controls reviewed and signed for the customer account (when applicable).
signoff_checklist: Security Engineering: KMS/HSM integration reviewed and approved
SRE/Support: runbooks present and reachable in runbook repo
Customer Success: onboarding playbook executed with customer
Engineering: any infra changes merged and deployed to staging (link PR)
Final sign-off email thread archived in onboarding folder

notes: Trade-offs: 1) Making audit export mandatory increases onboarding time but reduces residual risk; 2) Allowing shorter retention windows lowers storage cost but increases compliance risk for some customers.
Open question: Do we require Hardware-backed keys for all customers in regulated industries, or allow software KMS with compensating controls? (Security to recommend)
Performance impact: KV cache and tokenization paths must ensure key access latency stays below 50ms on average; ENG to validate under ENG-2081.
Fallback policy: When customer KMS is unreachable, runtime must support a documented emergency fallback key (customer-approved) or fail-safe reject; both options need legal sign-off.
final_notes: This document will be used by Solutions and CS as the canonical acceptance checklist for customers requiring customer-managed keying and extended audit retention. Any scope changes must be recorded as follow-up sub-issues and approved by Product Security.
